justification: Standard: rebuilds the bush fire prone land overlay and the lot-level bush fire flag from the state map. Not Minor: it replaces 235,798 production rows and rewrites a flag on lots. Not Critical: nothing in the served rules changes, the old rows and old flags are saved to files first, the swap is one transaction that refuses unless a 150-point check against the live map passed, and a clear in our copy is still confirmed on the live map.

pre_impl.existing_data: spatial_overlays held 235,798 bushfire rows loaded 2026-04..05; 804 live areas missing, 6,066 gone from live; lot_search_index.bushfire_prone true on 584,867 of 3,126,418 lots. Measured on 2,000 lots: 232 flags (11.6%) differ from the new layer.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: I counted staged areas by id and reported 6,522 missing; complex areas are stored as split pieces keyed 10^12 + id*100000 + n, so the real figure was 2,199. Separately the state service answers some large batches with an empty list, which the first version counted as done.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: The existing loader deletes before it writes and takes about 7 minutes per 500 areas. This stages into its own table, verifies against the live map, then swaps in one transaction; the lot flag script recomputes one flag with the index builder's centroid rule and writes only lots that change.
pre_impl.external_source_error: 6 live areas (ids 176076, 216529, 218402, 218452, 218453, 225279) return a server error every time; they are named explicitly on the command line and recorded in bushfire_copy.json.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_rebuild_bushfire_overlay.py tests/test_rebuild_lot_bushfire_flag.py tests/test_lmr_area_lga.py tests/test_refresh_bushfire_new_areas.py -q ; PYTEST_REAL_DB=1 DATABASE_URL=... python -m pytest tests/test_rebuild_lot_bushfire_flag_real_db.py tests/test_rebuild_bushfire_overlay_real_db.py -o addopts= -m database
falsifiable_check.fails_when: The swap runs with staging missing areas, a batch the service leaves empty is counted as done, the backup is a second table in the database, or the lot script writes a lot whose flag did not change.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Run on the real service: the first version staged 224,932 of 227,131 areas and reported done; the test with a fake service that returns an empty list for big batches failed until the retry was added.
falsifiable_check.observed_green: 80 tests pass across the bush fire scripts and area-check tests; 4 more pass for the lot flag script. Live check: 150 of 150 test points matched the state map after staging and 8 of 8 after the swap.

functions.name: missing_is_acceptable
functions.input: a list of live area ids not in staging
functions.output: whether the gap is acceptable and which ids were accepted
functions.if_none: an empty list is acceptable; more than 20 ids, or any id neither proven unstorable nor named by a person, is not

functions.name: backup_to_file
functions.input: a database cursor on the production overlay table
functions.output: the path of a CSV holding every old bushfire row and the row count
functions.if_none: no rows gives an empty file and a zero count, and the swap then rolls back because the delete count must match

functions.name: changed_lots
functions.input: lot id, old flag and new flag rows
functions.output: only the lots whose flag really changes
functions.if_none: an empty list gives an empty list and nothing is written; a NULL old flag counts as false

values.value: which lots touch bush fire prone land
values.read_at: spatial_overlays layer_type bushfire, lot centroid inside the area, written to lot_search_index.bushfire_prone
values.if_missing: a lot with no hit is set false; the old value is saved to a CSV first

queries.purpose: Compare each lot's flag with the rebuilt overlay and update only changes
queries.where_clause: WHERE lotidstring = ANY(batch of 2000); layer_type = 'bushfire' with ST_Intersects on the lot centroid, GiST index, 100 s statement limit

break_it.scenario: The swap deletes the old rows and the new rows then fail to insert or the disk fills.
break_it.what_happens: The bush fire layer would be empty.
break_it.how: One transaction: it rolled back cleanly when the disk filled on 2026-11-19, leaving 235,798 old rows. It also rolls back unless the deleted count equals the backup count and enough rows were inserted.

break_it.scenario: The flag comparison for a batch of lots runs past the 100 second statement limit (lots with very large shapes), so the query is cancelled.
break_it.what_happens: Without a fallback the worker retried the same batch forever and the lots after it were never compared, leaving old flags in place silently.
break_it.how: A cancelled batch is retried at a quarter of the size, down to one lot, and grows back after a success; progress is printed after every batch and saved, so a stalled worker is visible and resumable.

break_it.scenario: A worker is stopped or crashes part way through, then re-run, or two workers cover the same lots.
break_it.what_happens: Lots could be skipped, or the same lot written twice with a wrong saved 'old' value.
break_it.how: Each first character belongs to exactly one worker (tested: no group dropped or doubled). A worker saves its last finished lot after every batch and resumes after it; re-comparing a lot already updated finds no change and writes nothing, so the saved old values stay those of the first write.

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - after merge run the area check for a known bush fire prone address and confirm the note; spatial_overlays_bushfire_new is dropped once the lot flags finish.
